artists.biography:
Crippled Black Phoenix is a rock supergroup from the United Kingdom. Several musicians have contributed to Crippled Black Phoenix's albums and play with them during their live shows.

Members of the band used to play in other bands (including Iron Monkey, Gonga, Mogwai, Electric Wizard and others). In 2004, Justin Greaves began recording primitive sounds he had in mind for years. He was encouraged by Dominic Aitchison, and their ideas would lay the backbone for Crippled Black Phoenix.
Although originally having an unorthodox start, since all the band members were part of and busy with other projects at the time of the band's founding, Crippled Black Phoenix remained committed to staying together and forged their sound. The band writes what they call "endtime ballads," signifying both the slightly macabre nature of their songs and their unusual blend of styles as the final evolution in music. This blend has led to them being called everything from stoner-prog to freak-folk to doom.

Crippled Black Phoenix have made live shows a focus and have performed in unusual venues, using Victorian-era instruments in tandem with more modern instruments.

perplexity.description:
Banefyre is a post-rock album by UK dark prog rockers Crippled Black Phoenix, released on September 9, 2022, through Season of Mist. The album spans over 90 minutes and features an expansive, deliberately murky sonic landscape that draws from post-punk, goth, and experimental influences. The band's lineup for this release includes vocalist Justin Greaves alongside Swedish vocalist Joel Segerstedt, who made his debut with the band on the preceding "Painful Reminder/Dead is Dead" single, alongside pianist and synth player Helen Stanley and guitarist Andy Taylor.

Musically, Banefyre presents itself as an intentionally complex work that resists easy categorization, moving fluidly between post-rock, punk, goth, and accessible experimental sounds. The album features several extended compositions, with four tracks exceeding ten minutes and two extending well beyond that threshold, including the closing track "The Scene is a False Prophet" at over fifteen minutes. The production creates a hypnotic, dreamlike quality, with repetitive themes and layered instrumentation that demand repeated listens to fully reveal their structure. Standout tracks like "The Reckoning" showcase the band's signature building dynamics and demonstrate an English sensibility that balances heartfelt, working-class themes with dark elegance.

Banefyre received mixed-to-positive critical reception, with reviewers rating it between 7/10, acknowledging it as a supremely interesting and creatively ambitious work despite some reservations about its overall cohesion. While it did not achieve the same critical consensus as its predecessor Ellengæst (2020)—which Metal Hammer had described as their "most cohesive and emotionally devastating record"—Banefyre was praised for its willingness to take creative risks and was recommended to listeners with interest in post-rock, even as critics acknowledged its challenging and deliberately obscure nature.
